It can be really frustrating, sure but having a buddy to laugh with (or at you or vice versa) by your side between all the frustration, the yelling, and the chaos is part of the course of what makes this such a fun and addictive time. Mastering the patterns between each level, coming up with unique strategies, synergise and having good timing can be incredibly rewarding and fun. Frustrating, yes but really rewarding.

Overall, a banger of a Co-op game that i would recommend to everyone. Just don't play it alone, please.

[h3]Enjoyment: 9.5/10[/h3]
Overcooked 2 is about prepping and serving dishes before the timer runs out, except you will be working in kitchens that actively try to sabotage you. The best new feature over the first game is being able to throw ingredients across the map, and tossing food directly into a frying pan or a teammate's hands is incredibly satisfying when you actually pull it off.

The game runs perfectly on the Steam Deck. You can technically play this solo by swapping between the two chefs, but you absolutely must play this with friends instead to get the full experience. The stages can get frantic and chaotic very quickly and is overall easily one of the most engaging co-op games I've ever played.

I finished the story while playing together with my non-gaming girlfriend, and we managed to earn three stars on every single level. And honestly, she was the competitive driving force behind it!

What can I say? We laughed, cried, screamed, discussed, planned, shouted—and celebrated with plenty of high fives throughout our chaotic but beautiful cooking journey.

This game is an absolute blast, and I definitely recommend it as a party game to play with friends. That said, I don’t see myself enjoying it nearly as much when playing solo. It really shines as a shared experience.

I thoroughly enjoyed playing this game. Although it can be played using only a keyboard and mouse, I strongly recommend using a controller for a more convenient experience. The graphics, soundtrack, and overall gameplay experience were highly satisfying. The only aspect I found disappointing was the limited number of levels, which resulted in my partner and I completing the game within a relatively short period.

Given its current price, I believe the game should offer a longer in-game experience than what is currently provided.

[b]Cons:[/b]

★★★★★ 5/5 – Friendship tested, kitchen destroyed

Absolutely loved Overcooked! 2, especially when playing with friends. It's one of those games where everything starts off perfectly organized and then, within minutes, everyone is screaming at each other because someone forgot to wash the plates.

The chaos is honestly what makes it so much fun.

I personally did much better playing the PC version compared to the Switch version. The controls just felt more comfortable for me, and I found myself performing much better when trying to get those precious stars.

The expansions can be pretty pricey, especially if you want to get all of them, but I actually think they're worth it. They add plenty of new stages, recipes and ridiculous kitchen mechanics, which gives you even more reasons to come back and suffer—I mean, cook—with your friends.

Definitely best enjoyed with friends. Coordinating who chops, cooks, washes and serves sounds simple until the kitchen starts moving, something catches fire, and suddenly nobody knows who's responsible for the rice.

Lots of laughter, lots of screaming, lots of blaming each other.

And then you immediately replay the level because you were this close to max stars.
